Applied Materials Hardware Design Engineering Intern

Automated RF Gasket Cutting Machine

RF gaskets were cut by hand against a tape measure, so accuracy depended on who was cutting. This machine feeds stock to a set length and tells the operator when to cut.

A Raspberry Pi 5 runs the touchscreen and supervises an Arduino Mega real-time motion controller. Closed-loop stepper positioning uses rotary encoder feedback, so it stops on true fed length rather than step count. I also specified the full power distribution and terminal block wiring. Drag the photo to see inside.

42 minManual work saved per day

Applied Materials Hardware Design Engineering Intern

Automated O-Ring Cleaning Machine

A portable machine that washes and dries O-rings on a repeatable cycle instead of by hand. An Arduino-based PLC programmed in C++ sequences the cycle, driving stepper motion through the wash and dry stages and switching pumps and air through relay modules.

Deionized water runs through an inline filter for the wash, and a DI air knife handles the dry. I produced the production drawings and BOMs in Siemens NX with Teamcenter.

23 → 1.8Minutes of manual processing per part

Nanoscale Design & Manufacturing Lab, $840M DoD initiative

Less material. Same stiffness.

Mechanical design and electronics cooling for nanoscale manufacturing equipment, 2025 to present.

Material kept80%
Bending stiffness kept96%

Same outer diameter. Area scales with r² but area moment of inertia scales with r⁴, so material near the center carries little bending load. This is an illustration of the principle, not the lab's dimensions.

Undergraduate researcher Mechanical design and electronics cooling

Hollow support tubes and a copper heat sink

I redesigned the system's bolted solid support tubes as hollow sections. Because bending stiffness depends mostly on material far from the center, the change cut material use by 20% while keeping bending stiffness, with tolerances set using GD&T. Drag the slider to see why.

I also designed a copper heat sink in SolidWorks to replace an aluminum part. FEA showed a 6% thermal improvement, and I machined the final part myself on a CNC mill.

  • SolidWorks
  • GD&T
  • Thermal FEA
  • CNC machining

Academic project SolidWorks Simulation

Static structural FEA

A full static study on a three-bearing spinner assembly: meshing, fixtures, bearing-face loads, then reading the results. Peak stress concentrated at the bearing bores, and the minimum factor of safety came out at 1.4, which set where material could and could not come off.

  • von Mises
  • Factor of safety
  • Mesh convergence

3D-printed wind turbine generator

I designed and printed the blades, frame, and generator mount, using CFD on airflow and blade pressure to guide the blade geometry. An Arduino measures output voltage and flags proportional, low-speed, and overspeed operation.
